title: Meteor-Scatter Ping Activity
dataSources: APRS packets (`aprs:packet`), WSPR spots (`wspr:spot`), satellite passes (`satpass:prediction`), NOAA APT captures (`noaa:apt`), meteor-scatter pings (`meteorscatter:ping`), SSTV images (`sstv:image`).
app: Software-defined radio and ham-radio stations — APRS igate, WSPR beacon, NOAA weather-satellite (APT) receiver, meteor-scatter monitor, and SSTV decoder — logging to Splunk HEC via scripted inputs.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=meteorscatter:ping
| bin _time span=1h
| stats count as pings, avg(duration_ms) as avg_len by _time
| sort - _time
description: Counts the brief radio reflections off meteor trails each hour, an indirect but reliable measure of meteor activity day and night.
value: Meteor scatter detects meteors even in daylight and cloud; hourly ping counts reveal shower peaks the eye can never see.
implementation: Ingest meteor-scatter detections into `index=personal`; review hourly ping counts and echo durations.
visualization: Time chart of hourly meteor pings with average echo length.
grandmaExplanation: It counts the tiny radio echoes bouncing off meteor trails, letting you detect meteors even in daylight or clouds.
